defect.problem: The due-process suggestiveness holding can remain marked good law, but the record-level assertion says varies_by_point=false even though the disclosed page itself treats Stovall as point-specific: the Wade/Gilbert retroactivity holding has been superseded while the due-process identification holding remains good. That internal point variation should not be suppressed.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep good_law for the due-process suggestiveness holding, but set varies_by_point=true and add a point override noting that Stovall's Wade/Gilbert non-retroactivity holding has been superseded by later retroactivity doctrine.

reasons: The lake scope note supports current good-law status only for the due-process suggestiveness holding: "Due-process suggestiveness holding remains good law; reliability framework later developed in Neil v. Biggers / Manson v. Brathwaite."
The disclosed page states a separate Stovall holding has been superseded, which conflicts with the treatment payload's varies_by_point=false.
The negative progeny edges are proposed/mentioned, so they do not by themselves refute the due-process good-law call, but they reinforce the need for point-specific treatment.
residual_risks: The disclosed record does not audit every proposed negative edge to final point-level treatment, so the exact override label should stay limited to the retroactivity holding identified in the page.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Render the badge as good for the due-process identification rule only, with a visible note that Stovall is not globally good law across all holdings.
